addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	import Foundation
2	import ReachyDesign
3	import ReachyKit
4	
5	/// Which of this account's robots central can see right now.
6	///
7	/// The list is the online signal — central sweeps a peer whose lease lapsed, so
8	/// a robot that is off is simply absent rather than listed as offline.
9	@MainActor
10	@Observable
11	public final class YourReachiesModel {
12	    /// `Sendable` explicitly: nested in a `@MainActor` type it would inherit that
13	    /// isolation, and the preview listing carries one across to a task.
14	    public enum State: Equatable, Sendable {
15	        /// No Hugging Face account, so there is nothing to ask central with.
16	        case signedOut
17	        case loading
18	        /// Central answered and this account owns nothing that is online.
19	        case empty
20	        case listed([CentralRobot])
21	        /// The token was refused. Retrying spends a round trip to be refused
22	        /// again; only a fresh sign-in changes anything.
23	        case needsSignIn
24	        case failed(String)
25	    }
26	
27	    public private(set) var state: State = .signedOut
28	    /// Set when a refresh failed over a list that is still on screen. The robots
29	    /// did not go away — the request did — so the list stays and this explains
30	    /// why it did not change.
31	    public private(set) var lastRefreshError: String?
32	
33	    /// Changes whenever the Hugging Face session changes, so a presented screen
34	    /// restarts the load that belongs to the new account.
35	    private(set) var accountGeneration = 0
36	
37	    private let listing: any CentralRobotListing
38	    private let isSignedIn: @MainActor () -> Bool
39	    private var attemptedLoad = false
40	    /// Which request is allowed to write back, and whether one is running.
41	    ///
42	    /// Two are easy to have in flight at once — the screen's `.task` and a
43	    /// pull-to-refresh land on the same model — and central answers them in
44	    /// whatever order it likes. Without this the *older* answer wins simply by
45	    /// arriving second, which is how a list of robots turns into "none online" a
46	    /// moment after it appeared. Same rule as `RobotSession.connectionAttemptID`: a
47	    /// superseded request never writes back. An account change bumps it too, so an
48	    /// answer that lands afterwards cannot repopulate a list the account no longer
49	    /// owns.
50	    ///
51	    /// Named for the newest rather than shadowed by a local of the same name inside
52	    /// `fetch`: `self.` would be load-bearing there, and swiftformat's
53	    /// `redundantSelf` is exactly the kind of rule that decides otherwise.
54	    private var latestAttempt = 0
55	    private var isFetching = false
56	
57	    public init(listing: any CentralRobotListing, isSignedIn: @escaping @MainActor () -> Bool) {
58	        self.listing = listing
59	        self.isSignedIn = isSignedIn
60	    }
61	
62	    /// Drops account-scoped data before another Hugging Face session can see it.
63	    /// Incrementing the generation also restarts a presented screen's load.
64	    func accountChanged() {
65	        latestAttempt += 1
66	        isFetching = false
67	        state = .signedOut
68	        lastRefreshError = nil
69	        attemptedLoad = false
70	        accountGeneration += 1
71	    }
72	
73	    /// A signed-in account has pending content before `.task` gets its first turn,
74	    /// even though `state` has not entered `.loading` yet — which is the first frame
75	    /// the sheet draws, and it must not be an empty-state.
76	    var isContentLoading: Bool {
77	        isSignedIn() && !state.hasRobots && (state == .loading || !attemptedLoad)
78	    }
79	
80	    /// The screen's own load, on presentation. A second one while the first is
81	    /// still in flight would spend a round trip asking central the same question.
82	    public func load() async {
83	        guard !isFetching else { return }
84	        await fetch(showingSpinner: !state.hasRobots)
85	    }
86	
87	    /// Pull to refresh. Always asks — the user asked — and supersedes whatever was
88	    /// in flight rather than queueing behind it.
89	    public func refresh() async {
90	        await fetch(showingSpinner: !state.hasRobots)
91	    }
92	
93	    private func fetch(showingSpinner: Bool) async {
94	        guard isSignedIn() else {
95	            latestAttempt += 1
96	            isFetching = false
97	            state = .signedOut
98	            lastRefreshError = nil
99	            attemptedLoad = false
100	            return
101	        }
102	        attemptedLoad = true
103	        if showingSpinner {
104	            state = .loading
105	        }
106	        latestAttempt += 1
107	        let attempt = latestAttempt
108	        isFetching = true
109	        defer {
110	            if attempt == latestAttempt {
111	                isFetching = false
112	            }
113	        }
114	        do {
115	            let robots = try await listing.robots()
116	            guard attempt == latestAttempt else { return }
117	            state = robots.isEmpty ? .empty : .listed(robots)
118	            lastRefreshError = nil
119	        } catch {
120	            guard attempt == latestAttempt else { return }
121	            report(error)
122	        }
123	    }
124	
125	    /// A failure over an existing list annotates it; a failure over nothing
126	    /// replaces it, because there is nothing to preserve.
127	    private func report(_ error: any Error) {
128	        if case .unauthorized = error as? CentralRelayClient.Failure {
129	            state = .needsSignIn
130	            lastRefreshError = nil
131	            return
132	        }
133	        let reason = Self.describe(error)
134	        if state.hasRobots {
135	            lastRefreshError = reason
136	        } else {
137	            state = .failed(reason)
138	        }
139	    }
140	
141	    private static func describe(_ error: any Error) -> String {
142	        guard let failure = error as? CentralRelayClient.Failure else {
143	            return error.localizedDescription
144	        }
145	        return switch failure {
146	        case .noToken:
147	            String(localized: .reachy("Sign in to Hugging Face to see your robots."))
148	        case .unauthorized:
149	            String(localized: .reachy("Hugging Face refused this session."))
150	        case .rateLimited:
151	            // Central allows 1200 requests a minute per token, and retrying at
152	            // once turns a limit into a ban.
153	            String(localized: .reachy("Too many requests. Wait a moment before refreshing again."))
154	        case let .http(code):
155	            String(localized: .reachy("Hugging Face answered \(code)."))
156	        }
157	    }
158	}
159	
160	public extension YourReachiesModel.State {
161	    var hasRobots: Bool {
162	        if case .listed = self {
163	            true
164	        } else {
165	            false
166	        }
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	#if DEBUG
171	    public extension YourReachiesModel {
172	        /// A model parked in the given state. `YourReachiesScreen` suppresses its
173	        /// initial load in preview mode so the first frame is already final.
174	        ///
175	        /// `refreshFailure` is the one combination `load()` cannot reach on its
176	        /// own: a list already on screen, and a refresh that failed over it.
177	        static func preview(_ state: State = .signedOut, refreshFailure: String? = nil) -> YourReachiesModel {
178	            let model = YourReachiesModel(
179	                listing: PreviewListing(state: state, refreshFailure: refreshFailure),
180	                isSignedIn: { state != .signedOut }
181	            )
182	            model.state = state
183	            model.attemptedLoad = state != .loading && state != .signedOut
184	            return model
185	        }
186	    }
187	
188	    private struct PreviewListing: CentralRobotListing {
189	        let state: YourReachiesModel.State
190	        let refreshFailure: String?
191	
192	        func robots() async throws -> [CentralRobot] {
193	            if let refreshFailure {
194	                throw PreviewFailure(errorDescription: refreshFailure)
195	            }
196	            switch state {
197	            case let .listed(robots):
198	                return robots
199	            case .empty, .signedOut:
200	                return []
201	            case .needsSignIn:
202	                throw CentralRelayClient.Failure.unauthorized
203	            case let .failed(reason):
204	                throw PreviewFailure(errorDescription: reason)
205	            case .loading:
206	                // Kept complete for callers outside `YourReachiesScreen`; previews of
207	                // that screen suppress the request before it reaches this fixture.
208	                try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3600))
209	                return []
210	            }
211	        }
212	    }
213	
214	    /// Carries a chosen message through `describe`, which falls back to
215	    /// `localizedDescription` for anything that is not a relay failure.
216	    private struct PreviewFailure: LocalizedError {
217	        let errorDescription: String?
218	    }
219	#endif
220

1	import HuggingFaceAuth
2	import ReachyKit
3	import ReachyMedia
4	import SwiftUI
5	
6	/// Entry point for the shared UI. It owns what outlives a screen — the session,
7	/// the account and its robot list, the viewport, the running-app dock and the
8	/// router — and chooses between exactly two things: connecting, or being
9	/// connected.
10	///
11	/// The tab bar lives below this rather than in the app target because every tab
12	/// shares one `RobotSession` and one `ViewportModel`. The app target's own
13	/// developer screen is injected and handed to Settings, so it keeps owning that
14	/// screen without a tab or a nested tab bar.
15	public struct ReachyRootView<Developer: View>: View {
16	    @State private var session: RobotSession
17	    @State private var viewport: ViewportModel
18	    /// Where that viewport is drawn. It outlives the shell for the same reason the
19	    /// viewport does — a corner the user chose must survive a network blip — and it
20	    /// is read by the lifecycle, which is above the shell.
21	    @State private var floating: FloatingViewportModel
22	    /// One Hugging Face session for the whole app, restored from the Keychain on
23	    /// launch and handed down through the environment — the account outlives any
24	    /// one robot connection, and several screens read it.
25	    @State private var hfAccount: HFAccount
26	    /// The account's robot list, held here rather than built by the sheet that
27	    /// shows it.
28	    ///
29	    /// A `.sheet` content closure is re-run on **every** update of the view it
30	    /// hangs off, so a model constructed inside one is replaced by a fresh, empty
31	    /// one each time. This body reads `session.phase`, and the candidate sweep
32	    /// walks it `idle → handshaking → idle` every 10 s while the gate is up — so
33	    /// the list of robots the user was reading was replaced within seconds by a
34	    /// model that had never asked central anything, and `.task` does not get a
35	    /// second turn to ask again.
36	    @State private var remoteRobots: YourReachiesModel
37	    @State private var runningApp: RunningAppModel
38	    @State private var router: ReachyRouter
39	    /// Held for as long as the remote session is: dropping it would close the peer
40	    /// connection the session is talking over.
41	    @State private var remoteLink: RemoteRobotLink?
42	    /// What the gate's rail is showing. Owned here rather than by the gate because
43	    /// the fork below is what destroys the gate, and this is what defers that fork.
44	    @State private var progress: ConnectProgressModel
45	
46	    private let developer: Developer
47	
48	    @MainActor
49	    public init(@ViewBuilder developer: () -> Developer) {
50	        self.init(session: RobotSession(), developer: developer)
51	    }
52	
53	    /// Internal so previews can park the root in a phase a real connection would have to reach.
54	    @MainActor
55	    init(
56	        session: RobotSession,
57	        viewport: ViewportModel = ViewportModel(),
58	        floating: FloatingViewportModel? = nil,
59	        hfAccount: HFAccount? = nil,
60	        remoteRobots: YourReachiesModel? = nil,
61	        runningApp: RunningAppModel? = nil,
62	        tab: ReachyRouter.Tab = .robot,
63	        remoteLink: RemoteRobotLink? = nil,
64	        progress: ConnectProgressModel? = nil,
65	        @ViewBuilder developer: () -> Developer
66	    ) {
67	        _session = State(initialValue: session)
68	        _progress = State(initialValue: progress ?? ConnectProgressModel(initialPhase: session.phase))
69	        _viewport = State(initialValue: viewport)
70	        _floating = State(initialValue: floating ?? FloatingViewportModel())
71	        _runningApp = State(initialValue: runningApp ?? RunningAppModel())
72	        _router = State(initialValue: ReachyRouter(tab: tab))
73	        _remoteLink = State(initialValue: remoteLink)
74	        let account = hfAccount ?? HFAccount(store: KeychainHFTokenStore())
75	        _hfAccount = State(initialValue: account)
76	        _remoteRobots = State(initialValue: remoteRobots ?? Self.yourReachies(for: account))
77	        self.developer = developer()
78	    }
79	
80	    /// Central, authenticated with this app's own Hugging Face session — which is
81	    /// the only thing that makes a robot visible to its owner and to nobody else.
82	    @MainActor
83	    private static func yourReachies(for account: HFAccount) -> YourReachiesModel {
84	        YourReachiesModel(
85	            listing: CentralRelayClient { [account] in await account.currentToken() },
86	            // `.needsReauth` also carries a username, so the state is the question,
87	            // not whether a name is known.
88	            isSignedIn: { [account] in
89	                if case .signedIn = account.state {
90	                    true
91	                } else {
92	                    false
93	                }
94	            }
95	        )
96	    }
97	
98	    public var body: some View {
99	        Group {
100	            if isConnectedEnough {
101	                ReachyTabShell(
102	                    session: session,
103	                    viewport: viewport,
104	                    floating: floating,
105	                    runningApp: runningApp,
106	                    router: router,
107	                    remoteLink: remoteLink,
108	                    findRobot: findRobotButtonTapped
109	                )
110	            } else {
111	                ConnectGate(session: session, router: router, progress: progress)
112	            }
113	        }
114	        // Opacity and nothing geometric. Crossing this line throws the whole tree
115	        // below it away along with its `@State`, which is right — a new robot
116	        // deserves a fresh app list — but it means there is no shared geometry for
117	        // a matched transition to move between.
118	        .transition(.opacity)
119	        .environment(\.reachyDeveloperScreen) { [developer] in AnyView(developer) }
120	        .environment(runningApp)
121	        .environment(hfAccount)
122	        .environment(router)
123	        .modifier(
124	            RootSheets(
125	                session: session,
126	                hfAccount: hfAccount,
127	                remoteRobots: remoteRobots,
128	                router: router,
129	                connect: connectRemotely
130	            )
131	        )
132	        .modifier(
133	            RootLifecycle(
134	                session: session,
135	                viewport: viewport,
136	                floating: floating,
137	                hfAccount: hfAccount,
138	                remoteRobots: remoteRobots,
139	                runningApp: runningApp,
140	                router: router,
141	                remoteLink: $remoteLink
142	            )
143	        )
144	    }
145	
146	    /// The fork the old `robotTab` made, with one condition added. `.unreachable`
147	    /// stays on the shell side deliberately: a network blip must not pull the tab
148	    /// bar out from under a finger, and the robot screen already says so in place.
149	    ///
150	    /// **The progress checks only ever delay.** The displayed phase must first catch
151	    /// `.connected`, otherwise the child observing the transition could be removed
152	    /// before it sees it. `holdsGate` then keeps that final frame visible for its
153	    /// dwell. The model releases on a ceiling that depends on nothing (`maxHold`),
154	    /// so no state it can reach keeps the reader out of a connected app; and at
155	    /// `dwell: .zero` it never holds at all, which is why every reference image
156	    /// behaves exactly as it did before this existed. `.unreachable` bypasses both:
157	    /// a later network blip belongs to the shell and must never resurrect the gate.
158	    private var isConnectedEnough: Bool {
159	        switch session.phase {
160	        case let .connected(identity):
161	            !progress.holdsGate && progress.displayed == .connected(identity)
162	        case .unreachable:
163	            true
164	        case .idle, .connecting: false
165	        }
166	    }
167	
168	    /// Opens the relay session first, then hands the session a client that speaks
169	    /// over it. `start()` only begins asking central for a session — nothing has
170	    /// reached the robot yet, and the control channel's own deadline is what bounds
171	    /// the wait if it never answers.
172	    private func connectRemotely(to robot: CentralRobot) {
173	        router.showsRemoteRobots = false
174	        stopRemoteLink()
175	        let link = RemoteRobotLink(
176	            robot: robot,
177	            relay: CentralRelayClient { [hfAccount] in await hfAccount.currentToken() }
178	        )
179	        remoteLink = link
180	        link.start()
181	        router.tab = .robot
182	        Task { await session.connect(using: link.client) }
183	    }
184	
185	    private func stopRemoteLink() {
186	        remoteLink?.stop()
187	        remoteLink = nil
188	    }
189	
190	    private func findRobotButtonTapped() {
191	        if session.isRemote {
192	            session.disconnect()
193	        }
194	        router.tab = .robot
195	    }
196	}

1	import ReachyDesign
2	import ReachyKit
3	import SwiftUI
4	
5	/// The three ways to reach a robot, one segment each, under a rail that says how
6	/// the current attempt is going.
7	///
8	/// Two things stay out of the segments on purpose, and both are load-bearing:
9	///
10	/// - **Bluetooth setup**, because a robot that has never been on a network is
11	///   exactly the one keeping the sweep failing, and burying the way out behind a
12	///   segment the reader has no reason to open would be the wrong place for it.
13	/// - **`disabled` is applied section by section**, never to the form. It is
14	///   cumulative and a child cannot re-enable itself, so one modifier on the form
15	///   would take the Bluetooth button down with everything else — and the sweep it
16	///   waits on runs every 10 s forever when nothing answers.
17	struct ConnectionScreen: View {
18	    let session: RobotSession
19	    let progress: ConnectProgressModel
20	    /// Absent in previews and wherever the remote list has nowhere to be presented
21	    /// from, which is what hides that segment's content rather than a flag.
22	    var showRemoteRobots: (() -> Void)?
23	    /// Opens the privacy screen. Optional for the same reason as the list above —
24	    /// the sheet belongs to the root, and a leaf that reached for the router
25	    /// directly could not be previewed.
26	    var showPermissions: (() -> Void)?
27	
28	    @State private var browser: RobotBrowser
29	    @State private var manualInput: String
30	    @State private var route: ConnectRoute
31	    @Environment(\.reachyPreviewMode) private var previewMode
32	    @State private var resolving: String?
33	    @State private var showsOnboarding = false
34	    @State private var awaitedHardwareID = KnownRobots.pendingProvisionedHardwareID
35	    /// Resolved in `onAppear` rather than defaulted here: a default argument is
36	    /// evaluated in a nonisolated context, and both models are main-actor isolated.
37	    @State private var knownRobots: KnownRobotsModel?
38	    @State private var sweep: CandidateSweep?
39	
40	    init(
41	        session: RobotSession,
42	        progress: ConnectProgressModel,
43	        browser: RobotBrowser = RobotBrowser(),
44	        manualInput: String? = nil,
45	        knownRobots: KnownRobotsModel? = nil,
46	        sweep: CandidateSweep? = nil,
47	        route: ConnectRoute = .network,
48	        showRemoteRobots: (() -> Void)? = nil,
49	        showPermissions: (() -> Void)? = nil
50	    ) {
51	        self.session = session
52	        self.progress = progress
53	        self.showRemoteRobots = showRemoteRobots
54	        self.showPermissions = showPermissions
55	        _browser = State(initialValue: browser)
56	        _manualInput = State(initialValue: manualInput ?? KnownRobots.lastAddress.map(\.displayString) ?? "")
57	        _knownRobots = State(initialValue: knownRobots)
58	        _sweep = State(initialValue: sweep)
59	        _route = State(initialValue: route)
60	    }
61	
62	    var body: some View {
63	        Group {

247	        sweep?.standDown()

1	import Foundation
2	import Observation
3	
4	/// This app's own Hugging Face session: what it holds, and how it got it.
5	///
6	/// Deliberately separate from a robot's account. Signing in here is what makes
7	/// "Your Reachies" possible at all — it is how central knows whose robots to
8	/// list — and linking a robot is a second, explicit act.
9	///
10	/// The browser is not here. Opening a URL and receiving the callback belongs to
11	/// the UI layer, which has `ASWebAuthenticationSession`; this owns the parts that
12	/// have to be right whether or not a browser is involved.
13	@MainActor
14	@Observable
15	public final class HFAccount {
16	    public enum State: Equatable, Sendable {
17	        case signedOut
18	        case signingIn
19	        case signedIn(username: String)
20	        /// The session lapsed and cannot be renewed silently. The username is kept
21	        /// so the prompt can name whose session it was.
22	        case needsReauth(username: String?)
23	        case failed(String)
24	    }
25	
26	    public private(set) var state: State = .signedOut
27	
28	    private let configuration: HFOAuthConfiguration
29	    private let store: any HFTokenStoring
30	    private let exchanger: any HFTokenExchanging
31	    private let now: @Sendable () -> Date
32	    private var token: HFToken?
33	    /// The PKCE pair and state of the sign-in currently in flight. Held here so a
34	    /// callback can be checked against what this app actually asked for.
35	    private var pending: (pkce: HFOAuth.PKCE, state: String)?
36	
37	    public init(
38	        configuration: HFOAuthConfiguration = .reachyMini,
39	        store: any HFTokenStoring = InMemoryHFTokenStore(),
40	        exchanger: (any HFTokenExchanging)? = nil,
41	        now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = { Date() }
42	    ) {
43	        self.configuration = configuration
44	        self.store = store
45	        self.exchanger = exchanger ?? HFTokenExchanger(configuration: configuration)
46	        self.now = now
47	    }
48	
49	    /// False until the OAuth app is registered on the Hub. The pasted-token path
50	    /// stays available either way, which is what makes this an honest question for
51	    /// a screen to ask rather than a dead button.
52	    public var canSignInWithBrowser: Bool {
53	        configuration.isConfigured
54	    }
55	
56	    public var username: String? {
57	        switch state {
58	        case let .signedIn(username): username
59	        case let .needsReauth(username): username
60	        default: nil
61	        }
62	    }
63	
64	    /// Reads whatever the last launch left behind. Cheap and offline — the token's
65	    /// own expiry is enough to decide, with no call to the Hub.
66	    public func restore() {
67	        token = try? store.load()
68	        guard let token else {
69	            state = .signedOut
70	            return
71	        }
72	        state = token.needsReauth(at: now())
73	            ? .needsReauth(username: token.username)
74	            : .signedIn(username: token.username ?? "")
75	    }
76	
77	    /// The URL to open in the browser. Remembers the PKCE pair the callback will
78	    /// be checked against.
79	    public func beginSignIn() throws -> URL {
80	        guard configuration.isConfigured else { throw HFOAuthError.notConfigured }
81	        let pkce = HFOAuth.PKCE()
82	        let state = UUID().uuidString
83	        guard let url = HFOAuth.authorizationURL(configuration: configuration, pkce: pkce, state: state) else {
84	            throw HFOAuthError.notConfigured
85	        }
86	        pending = (pkce, state)
87	        self.state = .signingIn
88	        return url
89	    }
90	
91	    /// Finishes what `beginSignIn()` started. Refuses a callback whose state this
92	    /// app did not issue, and never stores a token it could not attribute.
93	    public func completeSignIn(callback: URL) async {
94	        guard let pending else {
95	            state = .failed(HFOAuthError.stateMismatch.localizedDescription)
96	            return
97	        }
98	        self.pending = nil
99	        do {
100	            let code = try HFOAuth.code(in: callback, expectedState: pending.state)
101	            let issued = try await exchanger.exchange(code: code, verifier: pending.pkce.verifier)
102	            let username = try await exchanger.username(for: issued.accessToken)
103	            try keep(issued.named(username))
104	            state = .signedIn(username: username)
105	        } catch {
106	            state = .failed(Self.describe(error))
107	        }
108	    }
109	
110	    /// The personal-access-token path: the way in without a registered OAuth app,
111	    /// and the way in for anyone who would rather not use a browser at all.
112	    public func signIn(pastedToken: String) async {
113	        let trimmed = pastedToken.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
114	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else {
115	            state = .failed(HFOAuthError.invalidToken.localizedDescription)
116	            return
117	        }
118	        state = .signingIn
119	        do {
120	            // Validated against the Hub rather than pattern-matched: a token that
121	            // looks right and is not would fail later, somewhere less explicable.
122	            let username = try await exchanger.username(for: trimmed)
123	            try keep(HFToken(accessToken: trimmed, username: username))
124	            state = .signedIn(username: username)
125	        } catch {
126	            state = .failed(Self.describe(error))
127	        }
128	    }
129	
130	    /// Forgets this app's token. A robot that was linked keeps its own copy — that
131	    /// is a separate act to undo, and doing it silently here would leave the user
132	    /// believing a robot went offline when it did not.
133	    public func signOut() {
134	        try? store.clear()
135	        token = nil
136	        pending = nil
137	        state = .signedOut
138	    }
139	
140	    /// The token to put in an `Authorization` header, renewed first if it is due.
141	    ///
142	    /// Renewal happens here rather than on a timer because this is the only moment
143	    /// that knows the token is about to be used.
144	    public func currentToken() async -> String? {
145	        guard let token else { return nil }
146	        guard token.isExpired(at: now()) else { return token.accessToken }
147	        do {
148	            let renewed = try await exchanger.refreshing(token)
149	            try keep(renewed)
150	            state = .signedIn(username: renewed.username ?? "")
151	            return renewed.accessToken
152	        } catch {
153	            state = .needsReauth(username: token.username)
154	            return nil
155	        }
156	    }
157	
158	    private func keep(_ token: HFToken) throws {
159	        try store.save(token)
160	        self.token = token
161	    }
162	
163	    private static func describe(_ error: any Error) -> String {
164	        (error as? LocalizedError)?.errorDescription ?? error.localizedDescription
165	    }
166	}
